clue.text: Cabin unknown secretary placed in church showing gall

indicators.note: things placed in something sit inside it, so the earlier words go within the church abbreviation

parts.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church
a hut is a simple cabin
algebra uses x, y and z as unknowns
PA is a personal assistant

explanation.surface: A churchgoer is outraged that a cabin-dwelling secretary has been given a church post.
explanation.walkthrough: Z comes from algebra, where x, y and z are the usual unknown quantities.
explanation.definitionFit: Chutzpah is Yiddish-derived slang for brazen audacity, the same nerve that gall describes.

clue.text: Juliet pares ragged stone

indicators.note: something ragged is torn and disordered, so the letters of the word before it are jumbled

parts.note: Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Juliet trims down a rough stone, as a sculptor might.
explanation.definitionFit: Jasper is an opaque, often red, variety of quartz used as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Fashionable bird losing kilo

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so a letter is dropped from the bird's name

parts.note: a chick is a young bird
K is the abbreviation for kilo

explanation.surface: A trendy bird has slimmed down by a kilo.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the K from CHICK to leave CHIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic is a French-derived adjective meaning stylish and elegant, in line with current fashion.

clue.text: One part of play involving books is untouched

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the pair of words before it wraps around the books

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books of the Bible
a play is divided into acts

explanation.surface: An actor notes that one scene of the play, including some books as props, remains unaltered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One part of play' reads as a single unit, but One and the act are separate pieces that the books split apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Something intact is whole and undamaged, exactly as it was before anything was done to it.

clue.text: First screening about to follow Empire broadcast

indicators.note: placing one piece to follow another fixes their order: the short word goes at the end
broadcast suggests scattering widely, so the letters of the word before it are scattered and reset

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
re is Latin-derived for about, concerning

explanation.surface: A film's opening night is due to be televised from London's Empire cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: The Empire, Leicester Square, is a famous London cinema that hosts film premieres, which makes the surface convincing.
explanation.definitionFit: A premiere is the first public performance or showing of a film or play.

clue.text: Straighten out a French divan around noon

parts.note: un is French for a

indicators.note: a word placed around another encloses it, so the divan wraps the noon abbreviation

parts.note: a divan is a kind of bed
N is short for noon

explanation.surface: Someone lies flat on a French divan at midday to ease their back.
explanation.definitionFit: To unbend is to make something straight again that was bent or curved.

clue.text: In this way sleuth uses envelopes

indicators.note: an envelope holds something inside, so the phrase before it holds the answer within its letters

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A detective's method involves using envelopes, perhaps to collect evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Thus is a formal adverb meaning in this manner or like so.

clue.text: Warm up poultry for infidel

parts.note: to heat is to warm up
a hen is a domestic fowl

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction: reheat the chicken to serve an unbeliever.
explanation.definitionFit: A heathen is someone regarded as having no religion, which is what an infidel is to the believer.

clue.text: Farm managed by Switzerland

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
CH is Switzerland's international code, from Confoederatio Helvetica

explanation.surface: A farm owned and run by the Swiss state.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one for raising cattle in the Americas.

clue.text: Subject head in charge

parts.note: the top is the head of something
i/c is the standard abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: An organisation chart naming the subject's department head who is in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A topic is the subject under discussion in a conversation or piece of writing.

clue.text: Futile as miles off

indicators.note: something off is wrong or out of order, so these letters need rearranging

parts.note: the seven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A navigator laments that being miles off course has made the journey pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aimless has no purpose or direction, so it is pointless, as futile effort is.

clue.text: Unfortunately I peter out going into a spin

indicators.note: something that goes unfortunately goes wrong, so the letters that follow come out in a bad order

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dancer confesses their energy is fading as they launch into a turn.
explanation.walkthrough: To peter out is to fade away gradually; the whole phrase is fodder, not a description.
explanation.definitionFit: A pirouette is a ballet move in which the dancer turns a full circle on one foot.

clue.text: Opened beer in shifting dunes

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it, so the drink goes inside the rearranged letters
shifting sands move about, so the letters of the last word are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone cracks open a beer while sitting among drifting sand dunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsealed means with the seal broken or removed, so it has been opened.

clue.text: Pat is evil when knocked back

indicators.note: something knocked back is pushed the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: bad means wicked or evil

explanation.surface: Someone called Pat turns villain once a drink has been knocked back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pat' looks like a person's name, but it is the definition, a light touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dab is a light, quick touch, just as a pat is a gentle tap with the hand.

clue.text: Singer is exposed while keeping it on

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the word for exposed holds the following pair

parts.note: bare means uncovered or exposed
taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer is caught naked while trying to keep their costume on.
explanation.definitionFit: A baritone is a male singer whose voice lies between tenor and bass.

clue.text: Bad actor has me missing final bits

indicators.note: missing the final bits means each word loses its last letter

parts.note: taken as written, before its end is removed
taken as written, before its end is removed

explanation.surface: A poor performer complains that a part has been cut, leaving out his best lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the last letter of each word leaves HA and M.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is an actor who overacts in a crude, exaggerated way, so a bad actor.

clue.text: Numberless mass milk producer upset

parts.note: M is the symbol for mass in physics

indicators.note: in a down entry upset turns something upside down, so the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: a dairy produces milk

explanation.surface: A huge crowd of milk producers, the dairy farmers, are angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Numberless mass' reads like the definition, but only 'Numberless' is; mass gives M.
explanation.definitionFit: Myriad as an adjective means countless or innumerable, too many to number.

clue.text: More certain about right conclusion being capitulation

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the comparative wraps around what follows it

parts.note: surer means more certain
R is short for right
the end is the conclusion

explanation.surface: A general grows more confident that the right ending to the war is to give in.
explanation.definitionFit: Surrender is the act of giving up to an enemy, the noun capitulation.

clue.text: Annoy heads of research and nearly kindle limitless enmity

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters, so only the start of each word counts

parts.words: research and nearly kindle limitless enmity
parts.note: the opening letter of each of the six words

explanation.surface: Academic studies that almost rekindle endless hostility are bound to irritate people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' and 'limitless' look like deletion signals, but they are just words whose first letters count.
explanation.definitionFit: To rankle is to cause lasting resentment or irritation, so it annoys.

clue.text: Initially drop less refined piece of furniture

indicators.note: initially points to the start of the next word, so only its first letter counts

parts.note: the opening letter
raw means crude or unrefined, so rawer is less refined

explanation.surface: Advice to get rid of the cruder-looking item of furniture first.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawer is a sliding storage box within a desk or chest, and in older usage a chest of drawers.

clue.text: Screen short, first class adaptation at last

parts.note: curt means short in manner
A1 means first class, read as AI

indicators.note: at last points to the end of the word before it, so only its final letter counts

parts.note: the final letter

explanation.surface: A review of a short film: a top-quality adaptation at last.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 meaning first-rate is written AI in crosswords, the digit standing in for the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain is a hanging cloth used to screen a window or divide a space.

clue.text: Cliff caught worn scrap of cloth

parts.note: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
a rag is an old, worn piece of cloth

explanation.surface: A climber's worn piece of clothing has snagged on a cliff.
explanation.definitionFit: A crag is a steep, rugged rock face, a type of cliff.

clue.text: Factory design taking time

parts.note: a plan is a design or drawing
T is the symbol for time

explanation.surface: An architect's factory design is taking a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant is an industrial works, a factory or power station, in a sense separate from vegetation.

clue.text: Slab of glass is tiresome thing we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a word's sound rather than its spelling

parts.note: a pain is a nuisance or tiresome thing

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a big sheet of glass is a nuisance to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A pane is a single flat sheet of glass set in a window or door.

clue.text: Head of acquisitions donated tequila ingredient

parts.note: the opening letter
gave is the past tense of give, to donate

explanation.surface: A museum's head of acquisitions donated a bottle of tequila.
explanation.definitionFit: Tequila is distilled from the blue agave, a spiky succulent plant from Mexico.

clue.text: Light aquatic bird following short path

the bird is following, so it comes after the path in the answer

parts.note: a lane is a narrow path or road
a tern is a seabird
